title: Persistence & Secret Plane
subtitle: Operational state lives in workflow.db; API keys and OAuth tokens cross a separate encrypted credential boundary
description: A two-plane architecture view separating ordinary workflow, execution, context, and team persistence from the credential path in which AuthService caches narrowly, CredentialsDatabase encrypts fields, and credentials.db stores only Fernet tokens plus derivation metadata.

sourceRefs.reason: Dependency wiring for Database, CredentialsDatabase, EncryptionService, CacheService, and AuthService.
Startup ordering: initialize credentials.db, load/create salt, then initialize encryption with the server-scoped key.
Authoritative async SQLModel service for workflow.db persistence.
Operational tables for workflows, node parameters/outputs, executions, context support, teams, tasks, and settings.
Single credential access surface and the distinct API-key and OAuth display caches; refresh tokens bypass the process cache.
Separate encrypted SQLite schema with metadata, EncryptedAPIKey, and EncryptedOAuthToken tables.
Fernet field encryption and PBKDF2-SHA256 key derivation at 600,000 iterations.
Plugin Credential.resolve path that obtains API keys or OAuth tokens through AuthService.
DATA_DIR-rooted workflow/credential database paths and API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY configuration.

callouts.title: Blast-radius boundary
lines: A workflow.db dump carries operational state,
but never the encrypted API-key or OAuth tables.

prompt.primaryRequest: Create a two-plane data architecture diagram that makes the separation between workflow.db operational persistence and the encrypted credentials.db secret plane unmistakable, including the real service boundaries and startup-derived encryption key path.
prompt.composition: Use two large side-by-side framed planes. The left plane is a short Runtime Services → Database → workflow.db flow with a blast-radius note. The right plane flows Plugin Credentials → AuthService → CredentialsDatabase → encrypted credentials.db, with a side cache, a server key feeding EncryptionService, and a refresh-token warning near the cache.
constraints: Keep workflow.db and credentials.db visually separate
Show AuthService as the single service-level credential access surface
Show the API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY and persisted salt as inputs to the encrypted-store design
State that OAuth refresh tokens bypass the process cache
Do not imply plaintext secrets are persisted
avoid: showing the unused credential backend factory as the active runtime path
